narrative: Material PL3__M7544772 exhibits erratic demand (CV=0.62, mean 1,918 units/day) with an unstable lead time profile (CV=0.81, mean 1.11 days) driven by bimodal supplier delivery patterns. The current SAP policy of SS=225 and OQ=225 is critically undersized, providing far less than the 95% service level target. A capacity-constrained (r,Q) policy with SS=3,482 and OQ=7,162 (capped from EOQ=10,523 by the 10,644-unit storage limit) achieves the service target at 94% lower total annual cost by consolidating ~2,217 micro-orders into ~70 optimal replenishment cycles.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding: EOQ 10523 reduced to 7162 (max_storage_units=10644 - safety_stock=3482=7162)
SAP safety stock of 225 units is critically below the statistically required 3482 units for 95% service level
Unstable lead times (CV=0.81) require careful monitoring; safety lead time should be set to 0.47 days in ERP

research_insights.selection_rationale: With erratic but continuous demand (CV=0.62), frequent transactions, and a low mean lead time of ~1 day, a continuous-review (r,Q) policy is optimal. It triggers a fixed replenishment of 7,162 units whenever on-hand stock falls to the reorder point of 7,319, balancing ordering frequency against holding cost while respecting the storage cap.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage capacity constraint reduces the order quantity from the unconstrained EOQ of 10,523 to 7,162 units, increasing annual order frequency from ~47 to ~70 cycles. This adds approximately $1,700/year in ordering cost above the theoretical optimum but remains substantially below the current SAP cost. If capacity is expanded, the EOQ should be recalculated.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (225) + safety_stock (3482) = 3707, which is well within max_storage_units (10644). No MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
